schema.description: Arriving at one place during a trip, a leg within the trip, one row in a records file (source records). It does not close the trip; values are the row's own text.

basis.description: Why the arrival date is believed, in the extraction's own words rather than the source's: the flight that brought Matt there, written as "<flight> <from>-<to>, <d Mon>", or "hotel booking" with its confirmation number where the source gave one. Absent on rows that rest on the stay dates alone.

by.description: How Matt reached the place when it was not by a flight leg: the service and where it went, as the source's evidence wrote it. Arrivals by air carry no by; their basis names the flight.

date.description: The day of arrival at the place. Sydney local date, YYYY-MM-DD, as the records row writes it. This is the fact time. The records row does not carry the place's own zone.

id.description: The row id the records file assigns, chosen once. The travel history writes it as <origin>:<trip>/<kind>, with the date and a place or route appended where a trip has several rows of a kind. This is the identity.

place.description: Where Matt arrived, usually "city, country", as written.

stay.description: Where Matt stayed and for which dates, free text as written.

trip.description: The trip key every row of one trip shares (departed, arrived, returned, flight), written by the extraction as the year and month of departure and a short slug. It names the travel.trip series.
